leads.author: Denis Golovkin, Flo Sku, 3.1415926535897932384626, Diego Schmidt, Sparky (rebuttals: Mahfooz, Artem)
leads.claim: 'Yellow blue primes' in dbbi: tokenize dbbi with 'be' as one token. Every prime token index 2..83 (23 primes) then holds a b/be token; highlighted form dBBiBfBhccBEgBihaBeBeihBEggegeBEbBgehheBhhfBaBfdhBEffcdbBfcccgBfBEeggecBEdciBfBffgigBEeeaBE. Reading B=blue=1, BE=yellow=0 in order gives 1111 0111 0011 1101 1001, which is the first 20 bits of the colored-cell (=URL LSB) stream. Token 73 stands in for the FEFEFE cell, then 2 more bits match; the last two cells (blue, yellow) have no counterpart. Claimed odds about 1:2^20. Side ideas: b/be act as flags that switch a table or decoding method (#60586). Use the prime sums 490/497/73 (first 25 primes split by colour) as shifts (#61259). Colour polarity can be flipped (#61501).
leads.reaction_rebuttal: Mahfooz and Artem: the tokens at indices 17 and 19 read 'Be' but must be parsed as b+e (not as be) to match, so the parse has a free choice; also 'you only discovered there are 24 b's'. Flo: those two are blue cells, so ignore the e. Denis: allow b-at-prime then e-at-nonprime and the first 20 bits match. Sparky: '1 in several millions, not coincidence, but WTF do we do with it'. Nobody found a use for it.
leads.our_check: Re-derived the token list. All 23 prime indices <=83 hold b/be tokens; lowercase b also occurs at non-prime tokens 30 and 52. The 20-bit match needs the non-greedy parse at 17 and 19. Known hint, already in prior ledgers; c37 item 4 tested dbbi vs the 91-letter sentence.

leads.author: Denis Golovkin, 3.1415926535897932384626, .//, S | h
leads.claim: The LSBs of the characters of 'gsmg.io/theseedisplanted' = 0xF73D92 (111101110011110110010010). The 25 colored cells sit at every 8th position of the 14x14 spiral reading: .// gives 0-based clockwise positions 5,13,...,157,165,173,177,181,189 (steps of 8, with 4,4 around the FEFEFE cell). So the colored cells are exactly the LSB bit of each URL byte: blue=1, yellow=0, plus the FEFEFE cell inserted as an extra between bit 20 and bit 21. Denis's '/2 then +3 -> 7B9ECC -> dbbi primes' step is a joke.
leads.reaction_rebuttal: 3.14: 'only blues can be primes', 'pattern is clear up to 20th bit', 'selection over two options, prime gap at most 5'. No operational use found.
leads.our_check: Reproduced. URL LSB = 0xf73d92. Counter-clockwise spiral from the top-left (down first) puts the colored cells at 8,16,...,160,164(F),168,176,184,192, colour string bbbbybbbyybbbbybbyybFyyby, matching all 24 LSB bits with F inserted. The clockwise variant matches .//'s list as 0-based. This makes 'Yellow has a number and so does Blue' = 0/1 by construction.
